subject: Dedicated capacity guidance: long-context KV usage + quantization tradeoffs
messages:
From: Ishaan Pillai <ishaan@helixworks.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — 15k token contexts, KV cache behavior

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo. We have a near-term POC that streams clinical notes into a pipeline and maintains per-patient history. A couple of clarifying items for sizing our Dedicated plan:

- Typical user session: 1–3 queries, but each query can reference ~10–15k tokens of prior context (we're concatenating summaries + last full reports).
- Peak concurrency: 80 concurrent active sessions, sustained 3-hour windows for a nightly processing batch that re-ingests docs.
- Model: planning to run an open 70B LLaMA-style variant (unquantized baseline) with Redwood-managed runtime.

Specific asks: 1) Rough GPU count estimate for a committed pool to hit 95th percentile latency target (<700ms for first tokens), 2) whether KV offload to host can be used without large latency spikes, and 3) quantization guidance — tolerance for int8/int4 in exchange for lower GPU counts (we can run evals but want an Ops recommendation).

I've attached a small sample of session lengths and token distributions (helix_context_samples.csv). Can someone from your capacity/engineering team run a quick sizing sketch for the deal? We're targeting an early Aug start.

Appreciate it,
Ishaan
Director of Platform Ops
HelixWorks

Hi Ishaan — thanks for the sample data, that helps a lot. Looping in Connor for the memory/KV math and Marcus for overall fleet recommendations; Laura will scope pricing/contracting options once we have a recommended footprint.

A few quick clarifying q's to speed the calc:
- Of the 80 concurrent sessions, what fraction are typically "active" (issuing >1 request in a minute) vs idle (holding KV state but not issuing tokens)? Any TTL or eviction policy you expect?
- Are you ok with occasional additional latency for the first token if KV pages in from host, versus always keeping full KV on GPU for lowest tail latency?

Connor — attaching the CSV. If you can sketch a couple of scenarios (GPU-only KV vs host-offload with warm-cache hit rate assumptions, and unquantized vs int8 vs int4), that'll let Laura produce a costed commitment.

Thanks — Soojin

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ishaan Pillai <ishaan@helixworks.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — Dedicated footprint sketch + KV math

On Fri, Jun 25, 2027 at 09:12, Ishaan Pillai <ishaan@helixworks.com> wrote:
> ... Specific asks: 1) Rough GPU count estimate for a committed pool to hit 95th percentile latency target (<700ms for first tokens)...

Quick sketch below — high level assumptions called out. I'll produce a short calc sheet (attached: kv_memory_calcs.xlsx).

Assumptions
- Model memory (70B) baseline FP16 KV + activations mapped to ~56GB GPU memory (kernel + model weights). This is typical for dense attention sharded layout on A100/H100 families.
- KV cache per token: ~0.05 MB/token (after attention state packing; conservative).
- Average context used per request: scenario A (full long): 12k tokens; scenario B (trimmed): 6k tokens.
- Active sessions: 60 of 80 are active during peak.

Scenario 1 — Keep full KV on GPU (no offload)
- KV per active session (12k tokens): 12,000 * 0.05 MB = 600 MB/session.
- For 60 active sessions => 36,000 MB ~= 35.2 GB additional GPU RAM needed on top of model weights.
- Total per-GPU requirement: 56 GB (model) + 35.2 GB (KV) = ~91.2 GB => requires 80GB+ class GPUs with some headroom.
- For target throughput and latency (<700ms first token), target ~6 concurrent model replicas behind a small per-rep batcher (to keep latency predictable). So committed pool: 6 GPUs. Autoscale to 12 for night batch and buffer (since batch throughput is higher).

Scenario 2 — Host KV offload with warm-cache hit rate
- If we offload cold session KV to host memory and keep a hot working set on GPU, assume warm-cache hit rate 75% for active sessions. For the 25% misses, the first token may pay a host->GPU page-in cost.
- Hot-set per session (recent window, ~2k tokens): 2k * 0.05 MB = 100 MB/session. For 60 active => 6 GB hot KV on GPU plus model weights => ~62 GB total => fits comfortably on 80GB GPU with headroom.
- Page-ins: average page-in cost measured in our infra is ~120–250ms depending on host/GPU PCIe/NVLink topology; with prefetch heuristics we can reduce the 95th tail impact. So warm-cache approach meets 95th <700ms in most cases if you accept occasional 200–300ms spikes on first token for cold sessions.

Quantization impact (rough):
- int8 quantization of weights reduces model memory by ~1.6x (weights only) and reduces inference working-set proportionally; int4 can approach ~2.7x reduction but with potential quality regressions for some instruction/LLM behaviors.
- Using int8 across the fleet: model weight footprint drops from ~56GB FP16 baseline to ~35GB effective; combined with host-KV offload this reduces per-GPU pressure and could reduce committed GPUs from 6 to 4 for the same 95th-latency target in Scenario 2.
- Int4 would allow even smaller pools (3 GPUs) but requires an evaluation run on your prompts; we recommend an int8 eval first, then int4 A/B on a subset.

Risks & mitigations
- Quality regression with aggressive quantization — run held-out clinical prompts.
- PCIe topology: if your chosen private deployment has oversubscribed PCIe, page-in times could exceed 300ms; recommend NVLink or direct-connected host memory where possible.

I'll attach the calc sheet and can run a small simulation (1h) against your helix_context_samples.csv if you give the green light.

—Connor
Staff Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — pricing/commit options

Hi Ishaan — following Connor's sketch, attached is a draft quote (RW-quoted-pricing-HelixWorks-2027.pdf). Quick summary:

Option A (performance-first) — keep full KV on GPU, no quantization
- Commitment: 8 x A100-80GB dedicated GPUs (monthly)
- Estimated monthly: $96k (list), includes 24/7 coverage and priority scaling up to 12 GPUs for batch windows

Option B (cost-balanced) — host KV offload + int8
- Commitment: 4 x A100-80GB dedicated GPUs (monthly) + autoscale to 8 during nightly batch
- Estimated monthly: $54k (list), recommend 3-month trial with int8 eval run included

Option C (aggressive) — host KV offload + int4 (post-eval)
- Commitment: 3 x A100-80GB dedicated GPUs with autoscale to 6
- Estimated monthly: $38k (list), requires int4 quality pass and SLA carve-outs for rare tail latency events during page-ins

Next steps: if you confirm Option B as preferred, we can turn around a 3-month pilot SOW and a DocuSign link; otherwise we can schedule a ~30min engineering call to validate page-in times on your infra.

Attachments: draft quote + sample SOW.

Thanks — Laura
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ishaan Pillai <ishaan@helixworks.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 17:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — recommendation and ops playbook

Team / Ishaan — my recommendation to balance uptime/latency/cost: go with Option B (host offload + int8). Operational notes: 

- Committed pool: 4 dedicated GPUs (A100-80GB class) pinned to the customer; autoscale policy to add up to 8 GPUs during nightly batch windows based on queue depth.
- KV strategy: enable host KV offload by default with a hot-set heuristic (last 2k tokens). Implement a per-tenant prefetch window: when session activity is detected, prefetch neighboring segments to reduce cold first-token cost. Expect 75–80% warm-hit after prefetching.
- Quantization & rollouts: start with int8 rollout to 20% of traffic; hold evaluation metrics for 7 days on clinical prompt set. If quality metrics pass, expand to full traffic. Reserve int4 as a later knob for non-critical batch workloads only.
- SLOs & fallbacks: 95th tail token latency target 700ms; on page-in events, degrade gracefully to streaming tokens while prefetch completes. Set an SLO exception window for the first week after go-live to capture baseline metrics.

I'll prepare a short ops playbook and a runbook for detecting and automatically prefetching cold sessions. Soojin/Connor: can you confirm the prefetch thresholds and add the runbook link to the Drive (I can review before SOW)?

Ishaan — we're aligned on an early Aug kickoff assuming pilot SOW by next week. Laura: please send the DocuSign for Option B and include the 3-month trial language.

—Marcus
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
